Hi Alex / Priya / Marissa 

Following up with more concrete details from the engineering side. TL;DR: Redwood supports the controls you asked about and we've attached a short matrix and SOC2 summary for review.

RBAC and least privilege:
- Roles: tenant-admin, tenant-dev, read-only-audit, support-lite. Each role maps to a minimal set of API permissions (describe below).
- Tenant-admin: can manage model routing, rollout, and billing views (not raw request bodies unless explicitly allowed).
- Support-lite: can open debug traces and request temporary session tokens only with customer consent or break-glass approval.

Support access & break-glass:
- Break-glass workflow: 1) Customer raises support ticket (Jira/ServiceNow); 2) Two designated approvers (customer admin + Redwood on-call lead) approve; 3) Temporary support session is provisioned (time-limited, scoped to a single tenant and set of request IDs); 4) All actions audited and immutable.
- Session tokens are single-use and expire in 15 minutes by default.
- Every support session requires a linked ticket ID and stores approver IDs in the audit record.

Audit logging & retention:
- Audit logs include timestamp, actor (internal email), actor role, action (read/describe/debug), resource id (tenant id, request id), and originating IP.
- Default audit retention: 90 days. Retention can be shortened to 30 days for EU-only tenants on request; long-term archival (365 days) available as opt-in.
- PII in logs: by default we redact request/response payloads. If you enable full payload logging we recommend tokenization or customer-managed encryption keys.

Data residency & isolation:
- We support region-scoped tenants (US, EU). Data in EU tenants is stored and processed in EU regions; control plane metadata may traverse control plane endpoints but can be configured for EU-only control plane for enterprise agreements.

Attachments included: access_controls_matrix.xlsx (role mappings & example audit entries), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (high-level controls and scope).

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa: can we schedule a 30m technical review next week to walk through the matrix?
- Alex/Priya: confirm targeted residency for production (US vs EU) so we can prepare a tailored configuration and any required addendum.

Happy to join the call  I'll bring examples of audit logs (sanitized) and a demo of the break-glass flow.

Thanks,
